subfield: Condensed matter physics / topological quantum materials and epitaxial growth
motivation: In 2010 Fang and Dai (with the late S.-C. Zhang) predicted that magnetically doped Bi2Se3-family topological insulator films would show a quantized Hall effect without any external magnetic field. In 2013 Xue's team found the effect in Cr-doped (Bi,Sb)2Te3 films: the Hall resistance was quantized at h/e^2 at zero field and the longitudinal resistance nearly vanished. This was the first realization of Haldane's 1988 Chern-insulator concept, and it rested on a remarkable feat of molecular-beam epitaxy. To see the effect, the film thickness, the magnetic doping and the Fermi level all had to be controlled at the atomic scale. The result has been reproduced around the world and opened the field of intrinsic magnetic topological materials. Dissipationless chiral edge channels are now being pursued for resistance metrology, low-power electronics and topological quantum devices. The work is a clear example of how precise crystal growth turns a theoretical idea into new physics.
